neutral_facts.value: The accused married the victim, and she gave birth to a male child. The victim filed multiple complaints against the accused for harassment and cruelty. The victim committed suicide by consuming tablets of aluminum phosphide within seven years of marriage. The accused was initially convicted under Section 498-A of the IPC but acquitted under Section 306. The High Court upheld the conviction under Section 498-A and convicted the accused under Section 306. The accused claimed the victim's suicide was due to her own pain and illness, but the court rejected this, noting the suicide note was not properly exhibited and the accused failed to inform the victim's parents immediately after the incident. The prosecution presented evidence showing the victim's suicide occurred within seven years of marriage and that the accused subjected her to cruelty.

appeal_history.value: Trial court: Convicted under s.498-A, acquitted under s.306. High Court: Upheld conviction under s.498-A, convicted and sentenced under s.306. Supreme Court: Affirmed High Court's decision.

quotes.text: Sessions Court, Hamirpur, H.P. after appreciating the evidence on record adduced by the prosecution as well as by the defence, convicted the appellant-accused for the offence under Section 498-A IPC

High Court vide the impugned Judgment and Order dismissed the appeal preferred by the appellant whereas allowed the appeal preferred by the State and convicted the appellant for the offence under Section 306 of IPC

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant had subjected the deceased to cruelty, which led to her committing suicide, and that the deceased had committed suicide within seven years of marriage, thereby triggering the presumption under Section 113A of the Evidence Act.

quotes.text: Prosecution by leading cogent evidence established that the deceased had committed suicide within a period of seven years from the date of her marriage and that the husband had subjected her to cruelty as contemplated in s.498-A

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the deceased's suicide was due to her own intolerable pain and illness, not the cruelty of the appellant, and that the suicide note was not properly exhibited in evidence, and the appellant had not informed the deceased's parents immediately after the incident.

quotes.text: Appellant’s case that as per the suicide note, the suicide was committed by the deceased on account of her intolerable pain and illness and not due to the cruelty of the appellant, cannot be accepted
Suicidal note not duly exhibited for being admitted in evidence, as also the appellant had not even bothered to inform the parents of the deceased immediately after the incident smacked of his guilt

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle under Section 113A of the Evidence Act, which allows the court to presume that a married woman's suicide was abetted by her husband or relative if it occurred within seven years of marriage and she was subjected to cruelty.

quotes.text: High Court rightly raised the presumption u/s.113A to hold that the suicide was abetted by the appellant
the court may presume, having regard to all the other circumstances of the case, that such suicide had been abetted by her husband or by such relative of her husband
